To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the proposed approach and toolflow enables the parallelization of complex legacy embedded applications, b) the parallelization of legacy applications is possible with minimal code modification and c) the proposed approach is suitable for the extraction of pipeline, task and data parallelism.

we have developed a new parallelization approach and (software) infrastructure for embedded systems that enables the extraction and implementation pipeline, task- and data-level parallelization for embedded applications on heterogeneous multi-core systems running distributed real-time OS.

the proposed approach and infrastructure enables fast and easy parallelization of legacy embedded applications for heterogeneous MPSoCs, while the combination of the parallelization, mapping, and optimization tools enables the efficient implementation of parallel applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
enabling the development of efficient and scalable parallel embedded software for future embedded MPSoC systems.
the following questions: How to efficiently support the parallelization of legacy embedded applications on resource-restricted heterogeneous MPSoCs?
enabling the efficient implementation of parallelism on resource-restricted heterogeneous MPSoCs for embedded applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach and toolflow is a promising step towards a more efficient utilization of parallelism in resource-restricted embedded applications.

the presented approach is able to extract parallelism efficiently from complex applications, to implement it efficiently on embedded systems with heterogeneous MPSoCs, and to optimize the mapping and communication to achieve high performance and energy-efficiency.
this paper describes a novel parallelization approach for embedded systems that allows to extract pipeline, task, and data level parallelism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new toolflow for extracting, mapping and optimizing parallelism for heterogeneous MPSoC architectures running embedded applications with distributed real-time operating system.
we have developed a toolflow that enables the fast and easy prototypic exploration of the performance potential of heterogeneous MPSoC architectures.
we have developed a toolchain that allows for the efficient extraction and exploitation of parallelism for typical low-end embedded applications running on heterogeneous MPSoC systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed approach and infrastructure is a first step towards a new generation of parallelization and optimization tools that can efficiently support the development of resource-restricted embedded applications for heterogeneous MPSoCs.
the presented approach and infrastructure enable a fast and easy prototypical parallelization and optimization of embedded systems.

we have demonstrated that the proposed parallelization approach is applicable to a wide variety of embedded systems, and can be applied to a wide range of legacy applications, while still achieving high levels of parallelism.
